seed.complete_norm_class_proof: The spatial Niemeier lattice is even unimodular. For primitive r=(x,y), q(r) divides 2I(r), I(r)=(a*x,(y,N)). Away from the ramified prime pi=sqrt(2), local unimodularity makes I(r) the unit ideal. The exact pi-adic parity argument is therefore identical to the E8^3 proof. Totally positive units are squares. For a=pi, the complete representatives are 2 and 2+pi.

control_seed.complete_norm_class_proof: Put pi=sqrt(2), so (2)=(pi)^2. For primitive r=(x,y), reflection integrality is (q(r))|2I(r), I(r)=(pi*x,G*y). The E8^3 block is even unimodular. Away from (pi), local unimodularity and primitivity make I(r)=O. If x is a unit, q=-pi*x^2 mod pi^2 and v_pi(q)=1. If x is not a unit, some spatial coordinate is a unit, I(r)=O, and evenness gives v_pi(q)>=2; divisibility by 2 forces v_pi(q)=2. Thus the norm ideals are (pi),(pi^2). The unit epsilon=1+pi has signs (+,-), and O*=+/-epsilon^Z, so every totally-positive unit is a square. The totally-positive representatives are epsilon*pi=2+pi and pi^2=2.
